title: WPSS/308/2017 of ASHISH NEGI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH SECRETARY, DEPARTMENT OF APPOINTMENT AND PERSONNEL

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 308 (S/S) of 2017

Ashish Negi ........ Petitioner
Versus
State of Uttarakhand and others ..... Respondents
Mr. Alok Mahra, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mrs. Anjali Bhargava, Mr. P.C. Bisht & Mr. P.S. Bisht, Addl. C.S.C. with Mr. N.P. Sah, S.C.,
Mrs. Indu Sharma & Mr. Narain Dutt, Brief Holders for the State.
Hon'ble Lok Pal Singh, J.
The present petition has been filed by the petitioner
seeking following reliefs:-
"(i) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of certiorari quashing the impugned order dated
22.12.2016 passed by respondent no.1 (annexure no.10)
and order dated 18.02.2017 passed by respondent no.4
(annexure no.11).
(ii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus restraining the respondents from
disturbing/altering petitioner's status from Senior Cane
Development Inspector to Cane Development Inspector.
(iii) Issue a writ, order or direction in the
nature of mandamus declaring petitioner as validly
appointed Senior Cane Development Inspector."
2. The facts leading to the present case are that earlier
the petitioner served as LT Grade Teacher (Agriculture) in
Government Inter College at Pauri Garhwal and was getting
salary in the Pay Scale of Rs.9300-34800/- with Grade Pay of
Rs.4600/-. The respondent no.2 invited the applications for
appointment on the post of Senior Cane Development Inspector,
Cane Inspector and Excise Inspector etc. in Sugar and Cane
Development Department of the State.
3. Since the petitioner possesses the requisite
qualification, he applied for the post of Senior Cane
Development Inspector in the Sugar and Cane Development
Department of the State. Thereafter, he was selected on the

2
post of Senior Cane Development Inspector and the
appointment letter was issued on 15.10.2013. The petitioner
obtained 'No Objection Certificate' from the previous employer
and submitted his application. He was relieved from the post of
LT Grade Teacher (Agriculture) on 21.10.2013 and he joined his
duties on the post of Senior Cane Development Inspector on
22.10.2013. Some unsuccessful candidates preferred WPSS
No.476 of 2013 (Reena Naulia and others vs. State of
Uttarakhand) and others with connected WPSS No.491 of 2013
(Mahesh Prasad and another vs. State of Uttarakhand and
others) before this Court, which was allowed vide order dated
29.07.2013 and the candidates who were declared unsuccessful
on account of not having the B.Sc. degree in Agriculture were
declared successful.
4. Having considered the degree of M.Sc. in Agriculture,
the aforesaid writ petitions were disposed of by the Coordinate
Bench of this Court vide its judgment and order dated
29.07.2013 and directions were issued to the State Public
Service Commission to declare their result. Feeling aggrieved,
the Uttarakhand Public Service Commission preferred Special
Appeal No.467 of 2013 (Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission vs. Reena Naulia & others) and connected Special
Appeal No. 466 of 2013 (Uttarakhand Public Service
Commission vs. Mahesh Prasad & others).

5. The Division Bench of this Court vide its judgment
and order dated 11.03.2014 dismissed the appeal and upheld
the judgment passed by the learned Single Judge. Pursuant to
the direction issued by the learned Single Judge, the result of
the writ petitioner was declared. Pursuant to the order passed
by this Court, the respondent no.2 prepared a fresh amended
select list/result on 06.05.2014. Respondent no.5 Shri

3
Amrendra Chaudhary was appointed on the post of Senior Cane
Development Inspector and while doing so, the name of the
petitioner was not recommended and he was pushed down to a
lower post, from Senior Cane Development Inspector to Cane
Development Inspector by the order dated 06.05.2014. Feeling
aggrieved, the petitioner preferred WPSS No.763 of 2014.
6. The writ petition was disposed of with a direction to
the State Authority that in case, such recommendations are
being accepted by the State Government, it is necessary for the
State Government before implementing those recommendations
which are presently under challenge before this Court. The
State must give an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner as
otherwise also it would be violation of Article 311 of the
Constitution of India. After giving an opportunity of hearing to
the petitioner, the respondent no.4 issued an appointment
letter in favour of respondent no.5 on the post of Senior Cane
Development Inspector, whereas, the petitioner was again
directed to be posted on the post of Cane Development
Inspector. Feeling aggrieved, the petitioner preferred WPSS
No.1706 of 2014, Ashish Negi vs. State of Uttarakhand and
others.
7. The writ petition was disposed of vide judgment and
order dated 12.10.2015 passed by the Coordinate Bench of this
Court. The representation of the petitioner was disposed of vide
impugned order dated 22.12.2016 and 18.02.2017 passed by
respondent nos.1 and 4 respectively, whereby, the petitioner
has been reverted on lower post i.e. Cane Development
Inspector. Feeling aggrieved, the petitioner has filed the writ
petition.
8. The learned counsel for the petitioner has drawn the
attention of this Court towards the fact that respondent no.5

4
Amerendra Chaudhary, who was given appointment in place of
petitioner, is already working on the post of Excise Inspector
since October, 2013. Respondent no.5 submitted an affidavit
before the Secretary Personnel Department on 03.09.2017
stating therein that he has been appointed in the cadre of
Agriculture Category-2 Service Section-B (Development Branch)
on the post of Agriculture and Soil Conservation Officer,
therefore, he is not willing to join on the post of Senior Cane
Development Inspector. Needless to say, the respondent no.5
declined to join the post of Senior Cane Development Inspector.
Therefore, the post of Senior Cane Development Inspector is
lying vacant. However, the petitioner was reverted to the post of
Cane Development Inspector. It is stated that the respondent
no.2 once declared its result and subsequently, pursuant to the
order passed by this Court, the amended revised list/result has
been declared. The Commission cannot act on its revised list.
The State has also filed counter affidavit denying the averments
made therein that the selection list has been revised pursuant
to the direction issued by this Court.
9. The learned counsel for the petitioner has placed
reliance on the judgment of this Court rendered in the case of
Manisha Verma vs. State of Uttarakhand vide judgment and
order dated 29.07.2013. The controversy involved in the
judgment (supra) is identical to the present case. Since the
petitioner is continuing on the post of Senior Cane Development
Inspector pursuant to the interim order dated 20.08.2017,
indisputably, the petitioner is not at fault. The petitioner joined
his services on 22.10.2013 on the post of Senior Cane
Development Inspector. Subsequently, pursuant to the order
passed by this Court, the amended selection list was prepared.
The fact remains that the respondent no.5 on whose behest, the
impugned orders were passed and as a result of which, the

5
petitioner was reverted on the post of Cane Development
Inspector. The respondent no.5 who has no grievance against
the petitioner and is not willing to join on the post of Senior
Cane Development Inspector, more particularly, for the fault of
respondent no.2, the petitioner cannot be reduced to the
position from the post of Senior Cane Development Inspector to
the post of Cane Development Inspector. It is apt to note here
that the petitioner was working in the Pay Scale of Rs.9300-
34800/- Grade Pay of Rs.4200/- and he was selected on the
post of Senior Cane Development Inspector on the same Grade
Pay.
10. However, having considered the promotional aspects,
the petitioner accepted the appointment in the pay scale of
Rs.4200/- but by the impugned orders, the petitioner has been
reverted on Grade Pay of Rs.2800/-. Since no fault is attached
to the petitioner, hence the impugned orders are unsustainable
in the eyes of law and the impugned orders are hereby
quashed. The respondents are directed to continue to the
petitioner on the post of Senior Cane Development Inspector in
the department from the initial date of appointment i.e.
15.10.2013.
11. With the above discussions, the present writ petition
stands allowed. No order as to costs.
